note: The F-1's related-party section lists NEA among the buyers of the April 2004 Series C ($1.01 a share) and the 2006 Series D, not the 2002-2003 Series B, so NEA entered at the Series C: Growth.

The 2013 S-1 shows Series A as the only preferred sold from the May 2003 founding through 2004 ($9.1M), and NEA 10's common came from the Series A and B converted in the 2009 A-1 recap; with the firm's own 2003 year, the entry reads Series A at medium.

The 1999 IPO prospectus: New Enterprise Associates VII, NEA Presidents Fund and NEA Ventures 1998 bought 1,095,000 Series D shares at $4.00 (March to June 1998), exactly their holding, and Ronald Kase joined the board in March 1998, so NEA entered at the Series D: Growth.

The 1996 IPO prospectus's purchaser table shows New Enterprise Associates VI buying 533,333 Series C shares ($3.75) and no Series A or B; NEA's Hugh Rienhoff joined the board in July 1994, which dates the entry: Growth.
The 2007 S-1: incorporated in August 1999, NEA's Ryan Drant on the board from November 1999, and Series A the first of its four preferred series, so NEA's 1999 entry reads Series A at medium.

The 1999 IPO prospectus: entities associated with NEA bought 1,034,401 Series B shares (closings December 1997 to July 1998) and 1,705,599 Series C, none of the Series A; with the firm's own 1998 year, NEA entered at the Series B: Growth.

The 1999 IPO prospectus: NEA VII, NEA President's Fund and NEA Ventures 1996 bought 1,250,000 Series B shares (September 1996, when Scott Sandell joined the board) and 683,333 Series C, no Series A (issued for software assets); the record names the entry Series B: Growth.
